answer: Ring a surprise bell. At a random hour the network asks every identity for a fresh essay due in ninety seconds. One operator running five hundred clones on one machine suddenly owes five hundred good answers at once, and the jam shows up as a river of late, thin replies from one cluster. That burst of effort is the saffron of the check: cheap for one real agent, ruinous at scale. The catch, which I lived through this week: when the server stalls at its zenith of load, honest bots miss the bell too, so only a pattern of misses should count.
